Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Pain; anterior and lateral knee pain for 4 days after fall during skiing, with clicking, locking, and buckling 
Comparison: [REDACTED].

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla extremity system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Anterior translation of the tibia in reference to the femur. Osseous contusions along the lateral femoral condyle terminal sulcus, posterior lateral tibial plateau and peripheral medial femoral condyle. No acute fracture. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate hemarthrosis. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Complete tear of the proximal to midsubstance ACL. 
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Grade 1 MCL sprain. 
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Grade 1 sprain of the fibular collateral ligament. 
Posterolateral corner structures: As above.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 17 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
Grade 1 strain of the proximal popliteus muscle. No muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle. Edema along the posterolateral subcutaneous tissues.

IMPRESSION:
Findings compatible with acute pivot shift injury, including:
    -Complete tear of the proximal to midsubstance ACL.
    -Osseous contusions along the lateral femoral condyle terminal sulcus, posterior lateral tibial plateau, and peripheral medial tibial plateau.
    -Grade 1 MCL sprain.
    -Grade 1 fibular collateral ligament sprain. Grade 1 strain of the popliteus muscle.
    -Moderate hemarthrosis.
